
{{alias}}( order, norm, N, A, LDA, work )
    Computes the value of the one norm, Frobenius norm, infinity norm, or the
    element of largest absolute value of an upper Hessenberg matrix `A`.

    Indexing is relative to the first index. To introduce an offset, use typed
    array views.

    The part of `A` below the first subdiagonal is not referenced.

    Parameters
    ----------
    order: string
        Row-major (C-style) or column-major (Fortran-style) order. Must be
        either 'row-major' or 'column-major'.

    norm: string
        Specifies the value to be returned. Must be one of the following: 'max'
        (the largest absolute value of any element), 'one' (the one norm, i.e.,
        the maximum column sum), 'inf' (the infinity norm, i.e., the maximum row
        sum), or 'fro' (the Frobenius norm).

    N: integer
        Order of the matrix `A`.

    A: Float64Array
        Input matrix `A`.

    LDA: integer
        Stride of the first dimension of `A` (a.k.a., leading dimension of the
        matrix `A`).

    work: Float64Array
        Workspace array. Only referenced when computing the infinity norm, in
        which case the array must have at least `N` elements.

    Returns
    -------
    out: number
        Norm value.

    Examples
    --------
    > var A = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 ] );
    > var work = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 2 );
    > {{alias}}( 'row-major', 'max', 2, A, 2, work )
    4.0


{{alias}}.ndarray( norm, N, A, sa1, sa2, oa, work, sw, ow )
    Computes the value of the one norm, Frobenius norm, infinity norm, or the
    element of largest absolute value of an upper Hessenberg matrix `A` using
    alternative indexing semantics.

    While typed array views mandate a view offset based on the underlying
    buffer, the offset parameters support indexing semantics based on starting
    indices.

    The part of `A` below the first subdiagonal is not referenced.

    Parameters
    ----------
    norm: string
        Specifies the value to be returned. Must be one of the following: 'max'
        (the largest absolute value of any element), 'one' (the one norm, i.e.,
        the maximum column sum), 'inf' (the infinity norm, i.e., the maximum row
        sum), or 'fro' (the Frobenius norm).

    N: integer
        Order of the matrix `A`.

    A: Float64Array
        Input matrix `A`.

    sa1: integer
        Stride of the first dimension of `A`.

    sa2: integer
        Stride of the second dimension of `A`.

    oa: integer
        Starting index for `A`.

    work: Float64Array
        Workspace array. Only referenced when computing the infinity norm, in
        which case the array must have at least `N` elements.

    sw: integer
        Stride length for `work`.

    ow: integer
        Starting index for `work`.

    Returns
    -------
    out: number
        Norm value.

    Examples
    --------
    > var A = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 ] );
    > var work = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 2 );
    > {{alias}}.ndarray( 'max', 2, A, 2, 1, 0, work, 1, 0 )
    4.0

    See Also
    --------
